summary: Round 2. F1 and F2 are genuinely fixed: `publishRun` is gone from SubscriptionHub.java and no other private member lost its only caller (`deliver`, `publishSegment`, `streamFromStore`, `writeHeldBytes`, `writeHeldBytesChunked`, `Target`, `EMPTY` all still have live callers). The three corrected claims are all true: the inline-forever config (Long.MAX_VALUE cap and crossover) makes `FetchPolicy.modeFor` answer INLINE for any size, so `HELD`'s length really decides nothing; `publishHeld` asserts no store count and the named `AssembledServingPathTest.aSegmentUNDERTheInlineCapIsServedINLINEAndReadZEROTimes` does assert `gets() - getsBefore == 0`; and both backlog-named cases exist and hold what the cell says (`aBATCHEDDeltaDeliversEverySegmentFromWhereItsBytesARE` compares 4096- and 8192-byte segments byte for byte, `aSTOREFailureOnOneSegmentDoesNotDenyTheSegmentThisPodHOLDS` really does order `seg-mine` second). The seven routing cases, the three moved callers and the clusterTest edits are intact and cost-clean: every call site passes the delta's own single segment key as `heldSegmentKey`, so `publishSegment` takes the INLINE arm and `serving.proxy()` is never touched -- zero object-store requests, no request scaling with records, shards, partitions or indices anywhere in the diff. What the delta did NOT do is sweep the tree for the name it deleted: three sites outside the diff still say `publishRun`, and one of them states a coverage fact this diff inverted.

findings.title: The javadoc of `aSubscriberWhoseOPENThrowsDoesNotDenyTheOthers` claims a coverage hole this diff just closed, and names a method this diff deleted
findings.failure_scenario: That paragraph reads: 'THE ONLY OTHER TEST OF THIS runs {@code publishRun}, the pre-M5.45a path M5.47 deletes -- so on the assembled path {@link SubscriptionHub#deliver}'s catch around {@code open} could be removed with {@code :ingest:test}, {@code :http:test} AND {@code :plugin:test} green.' Both halves are false after this diff. `publishRun` no longer exists, so no test runs it and a reader cannot even look the claim up. And the other test is no longer on the dead path: `SubscriptionHubTest.aThrowingSubscriberDoesNotStopTheOthersOrTheCommit` (line 131) subscribes `p -> { throw new IllegalStateException("consumer is wedged"); }` -- an `open` that throws -- and now publishes through `publishHeld`, i.e. the four-argument production `publish`. `deliver` (SubscriptionHub.java:366) is the only frame that swallows a throwing `open`; delete its `catch (IOException | RuntimeException slowOrDeadSubscriber)` and the throw leaves `publish`, leaves `publishHeld`, and reds that test. So `:ingest:test` would NOT be green. Concretely: whoever takes M5.48 (`pushLoop`'s silent drop) reads this paragraph as the current statement of what constrains `deliver`'s catch, reasons from a uniqueness claim the tree contradicts, and either duplicates a guard that exists or relaxes a test believing it is the sole one. The fix is one paragraph -- this is a stale-prose correction, not grounds for splitting the commit under review.md rule 12.

findings.title: Two more `publishRun` references survive the deletion, one of them in src/main
findings.failure_scenario: `SegmentProxy.streamTo`'s javadoc says 'This is {@code SubscriptionHub.publishRun}'s discipline and it is here for the same reason', and `SegmentProxyFailureTest.java:41` says '{@code SubscriptionHub.publishRun}'S DISCIPLINE, and here for the same reason'. The substance is still true -- `deliver` drops a throwing sink and serves the rest -- but the name is gone from the tree as of this commit, so a reader checking whether the two paths still agree greps `publishRun`, gets nothing back from any source file, and has no anchor for the comparison. `{@code}` is not a link, so neither javadoc nor `check-links.sh` sees it. One grep across the tree at deletion time is what the author's own F1 fix was missing; the replacement anchor is `SubscriptionHub.deliver`. (The `publishRun` mentions in backlog.md rows M5.12 and M5.45a are historical narrative and correctly past-facing; they are not part of this finding.)

findings.title: `assertThatThrownBy` is now an unused static import
findings.failure_scenario: Deleting `publishingABatchedDeltaWithONESharedPayloadIsRefused` removed the file's only use of `assertThatThrownBy`; the import at line 5 now has no consumer. javac does not warn and no configured gate catches it, so it survives indefinitely and tells the next reader the file still asserts a refusal somewhere, which is exactly the wrong signal in a file whose refusal test was deliberately removed. (`java.util.Map` at line 14 is also unused, but it was already unused at HEAD -- pre-existing, not this diff's.)

cleared: F1 fixed: `publishRun` is absent from SubscriptionHub.java; every remaining private member (`Target`, `deliver`, `publishSegment`, `streamFromStore`, `writeHeldBytes`, `writeHeldBytesChunked`) and the `EMPTY` constant still has at least one live caller -- `EMPTY` at line 358 in `deliver`. No import in the file became unused.

F2 fixed: the four-argument `publish` javadoc no longer links a deleted method; 'A removed overload took a bare byte[]...' is past tense and accurate, and 'THIS IS THE ONLY publish' is true -- `publish` has exactly one declaration in the class.

Minor 1 true: `new FetchPolicyConfig(Long.MAX_VALUE, Long.MAX_VALUE, 1)` gives `inlineBound = Long.MAX_VALUE` on both the same-AZ and the billed path, and `publishSegment` passes `bytesInServingAz = true` for held bytes, so `batchBytes <= inlineBound` holds for any segment -- HELD's three bytes are incidental, as the comment now says.

Minor 2 true: `publishHeld` makes no assertion about `store.counts()`; `AssembledServingPathTest.aSegmentUNDERTheInlineCapIsServedINLINEAndReadZEROTimes:81` asserts `store.counts().gets() - getsBefore` is zero and `modes` is exactly INLINE.

Minor 3 true: `aBATCHEDDeltaDeliversEverySegmentFromWhereItsBytesARE:281` asserts `fromMine.bytes() == mine` (4096) and `fromTheirs.bytes() == theirs` (8192) -- byte level, so a run delivered under the first segment in the batch reds it -- and `aSTOREFailureOnOneSegmentDoesNotDenyTheSegmentThisPodHOLDS:164` places `seg-theirs` first and the held `seg-mine` second, so a `segments().get(0)` shape leaves `fromMine` empty and reds.

No regression in the seven rewritten routing cases: each still asserts what it asserted before (own-stream push fields, no wakeup from other streams, both subscribers of a stream woken, close releases the stream and drops the empty list, a throwing subscriber does not stop the others, one delta touching two streams wakes each once, 1,600 subscribers all alive). `delta(...)` builds a single-segment CommitDelta, so `delta.segmentKey()` is well defined at every call site.

No regression in the three moved callers: `SearchableIT`, `ShardFanOutIT` and `EndToEndTest` each pass the same `key` they committed as `heldSegmentKey`, so the INLINE arm is taken and the store is read zero times; `SegmentServing(FetchPolicy, Capabilities, SegmentProxy)` and the one-argument `SegmentProxy(BinStore)` constructor both exist as used.

Cost lens clean: the diff adds no get/put/list/stat. `publishHeld` constructs a CountingBinStore over a MemoryBinStore per call (1,600 times in the fan-out case) but never reaches `serving.proxy()`, so the request count stays at zero and nothing scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.
